newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Talks on hostages release start in Tajikistan - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Talks on hostages release start in Tajikistan - Tass.

text.p: Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov started talks on Monday with a rebel group which is holding six hostages in his Central Asian state but prospects for the captives' release were unclear, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Tass said two members of the rebel group had arrived in the eastern Tajik town of Obigarm after a three-hour delay with one of the hostages, Tajik Security Minister Saidamir Zukhurov. It was not clear where the five other hostages were and Tajik officials were not immediately available to comment.

Apart from Zukhurov, the rebel group led by brothers Bakhrom and Rizvon Sadirov is holding two United Nations military observers -- a Swiss and a Ukrainian -- and three representatives of the U.N. refugee agency.
Tajik government officials say they have received promises from the Sadirovs not to harm the hostages and to release them after the talks with Rakhmonov.

The crisis erupted on February 4, when Bakhrom Sadirov's rebel group seized the first of the hostages and demanded that the government give free passage for his brother Rizvon and some 40 supporters to join him from Afghanistan.
The Tajik authorities allowed more than 30 armed fighters to reach Sadirov's base on Saturday on the understanding that he would then free all his captives. Only some of the hostages were released.
